message: Imported canonical English Task 2 fixture Context 'advisor2/structure' into profile 'task-2-proposal-authority'.

e32f543b-1637-572a-ab96-319d74ee7e21.content: Allow the problem framing to extend through a third sentence when a concrete person, setting, or use situation is needed to make the issue understandable.

6bbb0f69-ca99-539a-a810-a0fb34fe9cc3.content: Use the third sentence for the specific setting and consequence rather than compressing them into an abstract two-sentence summary.

48e887dc-7fc8-5a23-9999-890acb870251.content: Explicitly specify the users, operational stakeholders, and actual usage environment in the primary HCI research question.

e34bce0c-7d07-5fe6-b03f-39faa801640b.content: Provide one compact visual summary when proposing an unfamiliar interaction procedure.

68ad56f9-6ca2-587a-9182-fd98a79d3d5c.content: Mark the conditions that move an unfamiliar interaction procedure from one step to the next in its visual summary.

eca301ff-9feb-502d-b955-055c48342542.content: Present the master’s research schedule as phase-specific milestones for field understanding, system implementation, user study, and analysis.

cbd977cd-1b78-5ca6-823a-7a5b4b92d77a.content: Link deliverables that determine entry into the next phase to each milestone of the master’s research.

9283aedb-6818-5c99-8fe0-502b488acb66.content: Directly connect the gap in the actual usage context with the proposed design and operational contributions in a single flow.

c5c04ab1-10e8-52a3-98a1-aa9cbede57c1.content: Avoid extra subheadings in a two-page proposal; use paragraph transitions to preserve one continuous argument from problem to proposed response and next steps.

87203bcf-6724-543a-ad19-60a2becc4598.content: Begin each paragraph by connecting it to the previous claim so the short proposal reads as an argument rather than a stack of labeled fragments.

c9591180-6f3a-5909-8695-31704b9b6f01.content: Place preliminary results from field observations or technical validations near sentences supporting feasibility claims.

0ac685f9-e338-5549-bf91-32078cf36f15.content: This advisor has repeatedly seen readers misinterpret a compressed opening when the person, setting, or consequence is only implied.

5567fb3c-de90-5363-af1b-62fb5b8e0bb1.content: A two-sentence opening can become so general that readers understand the topic but cannot picture the situation the proposal intends to change.

32cef408-4c66-5ef2-9a59-eea6fc67b16e.content: Use paragraph transitions instead of extra headings when the repeated labels would consume space needed for the argument itself.

3579fcc0-c74e-5006-901b-6406a3106fa1.content: End each paragraph with the question or consequence that the next paragraph answers.

2c2aa1af-c450-5c8d-a907-042c5757d3ee.content: A continuous sequence of problem, consequence, response, and next step makes the relationship among claims audible without repeating section labels.

1fb62d5b-532b-5664-842c-57622e3c8b9d.content: This advisor has repeatedly seen very short headed sections read like an outline because each new label interrupts the connection to the previous paragraph.
